records.title: Advancing the SmallSat Digital Twin for Active Debris Removal Simulations

page_metadata.title: Advancing the SmallSat Digital Twin for Active Debris Removal Simulations
page_metadata.abstract:
:

The growing density of orbital debris threatens active spacecraft and future missions. While nets, harpoons, and robotic arms show promise for cleaning up debris, they are costly and demand precise control, motivating interest in space-based lasers that use ablation to impart small velocity changes for just-in-time collision avoidance and deorbiting. To mature this approach, we extend the SmallSat Digital Twin (SSDT) to provide a high-fidelity, spacecraft-focused simulation that integrates avionics, dynamics, core Flight System (cFS) flight software, ground control (OpenC3), and new radar/optical sensor and debris models. The enhanced SSDT supports realistic detection logic (Sun/Earth exclusion, field of view, limiting magnitude), representative tumbling debris with size/reflectivity parameters, and a laser engagement model based on an impulsive momentum transfer.

records.title: Digital Engineering for Cubesats With Semantic Web Technologies

page_metadata.title: Digital Engineering for Cubesats With Semantic Web Technologies
page_metadata.abstract:
:

Digital Engineering (DE) and the digital thread, which integrates information across the system lifecycle, offer transformative opportunities for systems engineering. This paper explores the application of DE principles to cubesat design and development, leveraging the Digital Engineering Factory (DEF) developed at the University of Arizona. The DEF integrates data from multiple engineering tools into a cohesive dataset using the Violet tool, which organizes the data as a graph database aligned with the University of Arizona Ontology Stack (UAOS). We extend prior work by applying the DEF to a cubesat design project. In particular, we develop a Python-based analysis to simulate orbital decay and calculate the time required for the cubesat to deorbit. This analysis uses inputs from multiple sources and is integrated into the workflow to demonstrate how the DEF supports automated traceability and checking of consistency, correctness, and completeness. This paper details the DEF's architecture, the cubesat application, and key findings, providing a pathway for advancing DE practices in cubesat design and development. Limitations and future research directions are discussed to guide further development of semantic web technologies in DE.

records.title: Digital Engineering Development in an Academic CubeSat Project

page_metadata.title: Digital Engineering Development in an Academic CubeSat Project
page_metadata.abstract: Digital engineering is increasingly introduced for managing and supporting the development of systems for space. However, few academic teams have the competency needed to manage projects using digital engineering and systems engineering. The subject of this paper is an academic CubeSat project in which a variety of digital engineering techniques are used. The tailoring that has been applied to fit the academic environment including students from different disciplines and levels of maturity is described. This paper shows how a customized Scrum methodology for hardware and software integrated with a workflow in a digital tool environment has given positive results for both the team and the system development. This paper also discusses how to introduce new members to the team and how to train them to work with digital engineering as a multidisciplinary team. This paper presents how the systems engineering and project management activities have been integrated into the academic CubeSat project, evaluate how well this fusion worked, and estimate its potential to be used as a guide for other digital engineering projects.

records.title: Digitally-assisted Development of a Space Robotic Arm for Small Satellites Applications

page_metadata.title: Digitally-assisted Development of a Space Robotic Arm for Small Satellites Applications
page_metadata.abstract:
:

In-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing (ISAM) expands space-based capabilities by extending satellite lifespans and decoupling spacecraft design from launch vehicle constraints. Robotic systems are proposed to support multiple aspects of ISAM missions, from capture and manipulation to manufacturing and repair. Consequently, the rapid development and testing of diverse robotic platforms is imperative to meet the evolving demands of the new space enterprise. This paper proposes a digital engineering framework to expedite the design, development, testing, and operation analysis of space robotic platforms. Digital engineering design tools are employed to optimize design for space environment operations; additionally, traditional manufacturing methods are streamlined with integrated wireless communication; IoT (Internet of thing) capabilities enable cloud-based modification to adjust to dynamic design requirements. Leveraging Amazon Web Services cloud-based servers, a digital twin of the robotic arm will be developed to assist the project's life cycle, from design to evaluation and test. AWS IoT communication protocols enable near real-time transmission of robotic arm sensor data to its digital twin. Siemens NX CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) facilitates photorealistic physics-based simulation, optimizing robotic arm control and motion planning. The paper details the digital engineering implementation of a two-degree-of-freedom robotic arm featuring piezoelectric rotary motors, applied in a zero gravity simulation air-bearing table study.

records.title: Multifidelity Framework for Small Satellite Thermal Analysis

page_metadata.title: Multifidelity Framework for Small Satellite Thermal Analysis
page_metadata.abstract: Anomalies, unexpected events, and model inaccuracies have detrimental effects on satellite operations. High-fidelity models are required, but these models quickly become large and expensive. Cheap or low-fidelity models speed up computation but lack accuracy. To compromise these requirements, this study proposes a multifidelity framework based on cokriging. The proposed multifidelity framework is compared against three other standard methods often used in satellite simulations: a standalone gated recurrent unit, Gaussian process regression, and the autoregressive integrated moving average with explanatory variables model. The robustness of high-fidelity data point placement is also examined. Moreover, the real-time aspect of the simulation is considered by applying the sliding window technique. This multifidelity framework is demonstrated using temperature data obtained from thermal vacuum testing of Small Demonstration Satellite 4: a 50-kg-class satellite. The multifidelity framework provided higher accuracy and robustness than the other methods, however, having a higher computational cost as compared to a purely low-fidelity model. Up to 92% reduction of the error was achieved by the proposed framework.
keywords: Keywords Geostationary SatellitesThermal Modeling and AnalysisGaussian Process RegressionArtificial Neural NetworkUncertainty QuantificationSpacecraft SimulationMultifidelity ModelingDigital TwinsCokriging

records.title: On-Orbit Digital Twin for Spacecraft Battery State and Health Estimation

page_metadata.title: On-Orbit Digital Twin for Spacecraft Battery State and Health Estimation
page_metadata.abstract:
:

Lithium-ion batteries are mission-critical for nearly every modern spacecraft, yet their on-orbit management remains dominated by conservative, heuristic flight rules that sacrifice usable energy and operational flexibility to avoid degradation. This paper presents a lightweight battery digital-twin framework built around a dual extended Kalman filter (Dual-EKF) coupled with an equivalent-circuit model. A fast filter tracks state of charge (SOC) at every measurement sample, while a slow filter estimates capacity for real-time state-of-health (SOH) monitoring. On-board battery capacity forecasts are correlated with periodic reference performance tests (RPTs) and compared to the digital twin prediction. The framework is validated in the laboratory on EEMB LIR-2032 coin cells and currently on orbit aboard the Proteus Space Mercury One spacecraft, which carries a dedicated cycling payload with three Li-ion coin cells. Ground testing achieves a voltage-prediction RMSE below 5 mV and capacity estimation within 2% of RPT-derived values; preliminary on-orbit results show consistent SOC convergence, capacity-fade trends in line with ground priors, and graceful behavior under telemetry dropouts. We also outline a short future-work direction: a Gaussian-process-based lithium plating detector that would add degradation-mechanism awareness to the digital twin, enabling operators to distinguish aging from damaging plating events.
keywords: Keywords Digital TwinsSpacecraft BatteriesUnscented Kalman FilterTelemetryGaussian ProcessProteusSmall SatellitesPolarizationConstant Current ChargingHysteresis

records.title: Test and Evaluation Procedure to Develop a Digital Twin of the Sleeper-Sat

page_metadata.title: Test and Evaluation Procedure to Develop a Digital Twin of the Sleeper-Sat
page_metadata.abstract:
:

A Digital Twin (DT) is not just a collection of static digital models at the component level of a physical system but a dynamic entity that evolves in parallel with the physical system it mirrors. This evolution starts with physics-based or data-driven physics models representing the physical system and advances to Authoritative Virtualization or DT through continuous data assimilation and ongoing Digital Engineering Test and Evaluation processes. This paper aims to create a mathematical framework for the DE Test and Evaluation Process, which incorporates data assimilation to link physical and digital models, uncertainty quantification, uncertainty propagation, and DT calibration process. This framework will enable the DT to perform operations, control, decision-making, and predictions at scale. The framework will be implemented to develop the DT of the Sleeper-sat to analyze the Sleeper-sat's structural deformation during its deployment in space. The Sleeper-sat will be a variant of previously constructed Sleeper-sats from the Aerospace Center at UTEP. The DT of the Sleeper-sat will be capable of predicting and monitoring structural health during its space operations.

records.title: Applying Program Theory Innovation Model for ECLSS Development for India’s Gaganyaan Human Space Flight Program

page_metadata.title: Applying Program Theory Innovation Model for ECLSS Development for India’s Gaganyaan Human Space Flight Program
page_metadata.abstract:
:

The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) implements the national space activities under the policy direction of the Space Commission constituted within the Department of Space (DoS), Government of India that directly reports to the Prime Minister of India. The stated vision of ISRO is to “Harness, sustain and augment space technology for national development, while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration.” Over the past five decades, ISRO has established India as a leading spacefaring nation through the Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites program for civilian earth observation and disaster management, the Indian National Satellites (INSAT) program for telecommunications and broadband network, Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), and through dedicated planetary and astronomy space science missions. In 2018, the Indian government committed the nation to pursuing human spaceflight with a budget allocation of ₹10,000 Crores (~ $1.4 billion) and subsequently provide a net additional funding of ₹11,170 Crore in 2024, with the objective to spur R&D in the nation and enable India to participate in future global space exploration endeavors for national benefits. In January 2019, ISRO established the Human Space Flight Center (HSFC) and is currently embarking on an ambitious ‘Gaganyaan’ program to realize human spaceflight capabilities within the nation, to undertake a crewed mission by 2027-28 to carry a crew of up to three to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) for up to three days and return them safely to Indian sea waters and from 2028 to begin missions to establish the Indian Space Station, ‘Bharatiya Antariksh Station’ (BAS), in a circular Low Earth Orbit (LEO) of about 400-450 km by 2035. The Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) that provides a safe and habitable environment for Crew Health & Performance (CHP) in the harsh conditions of space is the most critical component for any human spaceflight (HSF) mission. The development of ECLSS is a strategic capability in the space domain that only a few countries have achieved. In this paper, I provide the stakeholder & technical requirements and the structure of the major ECLSS subsystems through MBSE SysML diagrams. Given the significance and novel nature of ECLSS development for India’s emerging human spaceflight program, I then applied the innovation model from program theory to develop and understand the outcomes chain for the ECLSS Innovation.

records.title: Storm Classification and Dynamic Targeting for a Smart Ice Cloud Sensing Satellite

page_metadata.title: Storm Classification and Dynamic Targeting for a Smart Ice Cloud Sensing Satellite
page_metadata.abstract: Smart Ice Cloud Sensing (SMICES) is a small-sat concept in which a radar intelligently targets ice storms based on information collected by a look-ahead radiometer. Often, space observations are performed by continuously collecting data from an instrument aimed at nadir (e.g., directly below the space platform). However, if the platform has the ability to assess science utility of features that will be overflown, an intelligent measurement scheme can improve science return. In the case of SMICES, power constraints and the rarity of storms mean that with blind nadir targeting SMICES would collect a limited amount of ice-storm radar data. The work proposed acquires measurements to maximize acquired high-interest storms while concurrently collecting a background sampling of all features. This is accomplished through two steps: storm classification and dynamic targeting. For classification, we describe a multistep use of machine learning and digital twin of Earth’s atmosphere to create a classifier. We discuss an autonomous data labeling pipeline used to train five different models to identify storms in tropical and nontropical regions and assess the results and impact of expected noise. For dynamic targeting, six algorithms, ranging from “blind” to more selective, are described and evaluated on their improvement over “blind” targeting.

records.title: Architectural Optimization Framework for Earth-Observing Heterogeneous Constellations: Marine Weather Forecast Case

page_metadata.title: Architectural Optimization Framework for Earth-Observing Heterogeneous Constellations: Marine Weather Forecast Case
page_metadata.abstract: Earth observation satellite programs are currently facing, for some applications, the need to deliver hourly revisit times, subkilometric spatial resolutions, and near-real-time data access times. These stringent requirements, combined with the consolidation of small-satellite platforms and novel distributed architecture approaches, are stressing the need to study the design of new, heterogeneous, and heavily networked satellite systems that can potentially replace or complement traditional space assets. In this context, this paper presents partial results from ONION, a research project devoted to studying distributed satellite systems and their architecting characteristics. A design-oriented framework that allows selecting optimal architectures for the given user needs is presented in this paper. The framework has been used in the study of a strategic use-case and its results are hereby presented. From an initial design space of 5586 potential architectures, the framework has been able to preselect 28 candidate designs by an exhaustive analysis of their performance and by quantifying their quality attributes. This very exploration of architectures and the characteristics of the solution space are presented in this paper along with the selected solution and the results of a detailed performance analysis.

records.title: Analytical Modeling Framework and Applications for Space Communication Networks

page_metadata.title: Analytical Modeling Framework and Applications for Space Communication Networks
page_metadata.abstract: There is a growing number of resource-constrained small satellites that are currently performing and are proposed to accomplish novel science and technology missions. These missions seek to download large quantities of data to ground-station networks that currently have limited ability to support these missions. This limitation motivates the development of modeling and simulation tools to assess and optimize these mission scenarios. In this paper, we develop an extensible, analytical modeling framework for satellite operations. This framework captures dynamic states, subsystem functions, and interactions of the satellite with the external environment and ground-communication networks. This foundational framework enables assessment and optimization of complex space and ground networks under both deterministic and stochastic conditions. We apply this framework to develop a communication-focused model for an operational satellite mission. We implement the analytical model in a simulation environment and use realistic data from the surveyed small-satellite and ground-station community to assess the impact of satellite and network parameters on the potential for communication. Our simulations compare satellite downlink requirements and objectives with the constraint-based communication potential of diverse missions and ground networks. These results identify deficient and excess capabilities and motivate the need for optimal scheduling algorithms.
